target: Part III VR-headset pupillometry lighting-confound caution
note: P/anticipatory-application -- the review's explicit pupil-reliability caveats (illumination, temperature/humidity, age, camera-angle) caution that a VR headset's internal IR illumination and enclosed optical path likely substitutes for, rather than eliminates, the ambient-lighting confound flagged for screen-based setups; any future VR pupillometry channel should anticipate an altered, not absent, version of this confound.

P/anticipatory-application -- the review's quantitative eye-only-versus-multimodal contrast (71.5-78.64% vs. 81.76-87.55% average accuracy) suggests eye-tracking alone may suffice for binary boredom/non-boredom discrimination in a future VR study, but multiclass or graded boredom-intensity discrimination would likely require pairing eye-tracking with an additional biosignal channel (EEG or HR), echoing this cluster's Strand D EEG units' own methodological choices.

target: Part III self-report/physiology convergent-validity caution (STEM-methodological support)
note: P/anticipatory-application -- the review's categorical framing of 'subjective,' 'performance,' and 'physiological' measurement as three distinct, only loosely coordinated workload-assessment types lends independent STEM-methodological support to this cluster's bor-sec-28 (Kim et al.) caution against assuming convergence between self-report and physiological/behavioral boredom indices.
